exact_supplier_export.text:
Let $X$ be a finite nonempty classical label set, represented by a register $H_X$ with computational orthonormal basis $(\xi_x)_{x\in X}$ ([[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]]). For each $x$, write $\Pi_xz:=\langle z,\xi_x\rangle\xi_x$, the rank-one orthogonal projection using the root linear-first convention, as in [[lem-it-finite-cq-block-sum-is-a-state]]. Let $H_B$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space. A finite **classical-quantum state** is

$$\rho_{XB}:=\sum_{x\in X}p_x\Pi_x\otimes\rho_x,$$

where $p_x\ge0$, $\sum_xp_x=1$, and each $\rho_x$ is a density operator on $H_B$. It is a density operator by [[lem-it-finite-cq-block-sum-is-a-state]]. Its quantum marginal is $\bar\rho_B:=\sum_xp_x\rho_x=\operatorname{Tr}_X\rho_{XB}$ by the second-factor partial-trace formula in [[def-qc-partial-trace]], and it is a density operator by [[lem-it-partial-traces-of-a-state-are-states]]. The **Holevo information** of this ensemble is

$$\chi(\{p_x,\rho_x\}_{x\in X}):=S(\bar\rho_B)-\sum_{x:p_x>0}p_xS(\rho_x),$$

where zero-probability branches contribute nothing. This is measured in nats under [[def-it-von-neumann-entropy]].

exact_consumer_facts: [F1] [[def-it-classical-quantum-state-and-holevo-information]]: the ensemble Holevo information is the entropy of the average state minus the average output entropy.
actual_proof_uses: 1.1 The average state is $I/2$, while each individual state is pure. By [F1] and [F5], its Holevo information is $S(I/2)-0=\ln2$ nats. [F1, F5, given, algebra]

exact_supplier_export.text:
Let $X$ be a finite nonempty set, let $(p_x)$ be a probability vector, let $\rho_x$ be density operators on a nonzero finite-dimensional space $H_B$, and let $\bar\rho:=\sum_xp_x\rho_x$. For a finite POVM $(E_y)_{y\in Y}$ on $H_B$, define $w(y\mid x):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_xE_y)$, $q_y:=\sum_xp_xw(y\mid x)$, and the classical mutual information

$$I(X:Y):=\sum_{x,y:p_xw(y\mid x)>0}p_xw(y\mid x)\ln\frac{w(y\mid x)}{q_y}.$$

Then

$$I(X:Y)\le\chi(\{p_x,\rho_x\})=S(\bar\rho)-\sum_{x:p_x>0}p_xS(\rho_x).$$

exact_consumer_facts: [F4] [[thm-it-holevo-measurement-bound]]: every finite POVM has classical mutual information at most the ensemble Holevo information.
actual_proof_uses: 2.1 For either input $|0\rangle$ or $|1\rangle$, the squared inner products with $|+\rangle$ and $|-\rangle$ are both $1/2$ by [F3]. Hence every joint input-output probability is $1/4$, and each marginal probability is $1/2$. The finite mutual-information sum in [F2] is therefore $\sum_{x,y}(1/4)\ln((1/4)/((1/2)(1/2)))=0$. This is strictly below $\ln2$ from step 1.1, while still satisfying the Holevo upper bound [F4]. [F2, F3, F4, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

Let $\mathcal X$ be a finite nonempty input alphabet and let $H_B$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space. A **finite-input cq channel** is a map $x\mapsto\rho_x$ assigning a density operator ([[def-qc-density-operator]]) $\rho_x$ on $H_B$ to each $x\in\mathcal X$. exact_supplier_export.text:
For a finite bipartite state $\rho_{AB}$ on the ordered product $H_A\otimes H_B$, write $\rho_A=\operatorname{Tr}_B\rho_{AB}$ and $\rho_B=\operatorname{Tr}_A\rho_{AB}$, using the partial traces in [[def-qc-partial-trace]] and [[def-qc-first-factor-partial-trace]]. They are states by [[lem-it-partial-traces-of-a-state-are-states]]. Define

$$S(A)_\rho:=S(\rho_A),\qquad S(A\mid B)_\rho:=S(\rho_{AB})-S(\rho_B),\qquad I(A:B)_\rho:=S(\rho_A)+S(\rho_B)-S(\rho_{AB}).$$

For a finite tripartite state $\rho_{ABC}$ on the ordered product $H_A\otimes H_B\otimes H_C$, set $\rho_{AB}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_C}\rho_{ABC}$ after identifying the factors as $(H_A\otimes H_B)\otimes H_C$, and $\rho_{BC}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_A}\rho_{ABC}$ after identifying them as $H_A\otimes(H_B\otimes H_C)$. Let $P:H_A\otimes H_B\otimes H_C\to H_A\otimes H_C\otimes H_B$ be the wire permutation taking factor order $A,B,C$ to $A,C,B$ ([[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]], [[thm-qc-wire-permutation-is-unitary]]) whose unique adjoint $P^*$ exists by [[thm-adjoint-exists-and-is-unique-in-finite-dimension]], and set $\rho_{AC}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_B}(P\rho_{ABC}P^*)$, tracing out the last factor. Because $P$ is unitary, $P\rho_{ABC}P^*$ is a state: unitary conjugation preserves non-negativity by the adjoint identity ([[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]], [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]) and preserves trace by cyclicity ([[thm-trace-of-ab-equals-trace-of-ba]]). Finally set $\rho_C:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_B}\rho_{BC}$. All these marginals are density operators by applying [[lem-it-partial-traces-of-a-state-are-states]] after grouping factors. Define

$$I(A:B\mid C)_\rho:=S(\rho_{AC})+S(\rho_{BC})-S(\rho_C)-S(\rho_{ABC}).$$

These are finite-dimensional definitions only; no non-negativity of conditional entropy or conditional mutual information is part of the notation.

definition_or_statement_use.text:
Fix a finite-input cq channel as in [[def-it-classical-quantum-memoryless-channel]]. For integers $n,M\ge1$, an $(n,M)$ **cq block code** consists of a deterministic encoder $m\mapsto x^n(m)\in\mathcal X^n$ for $m\in[M]:=\{1,\ldots,M\}$ and a finite POVM ([[def-qc-povm-and-outcome-law]]) $(\Lambda_m)_{m\in[M]}$ on $H_B^{\otimes n}$. Under a uniform message, its **average block error** is
$$e_n:=\frac1M\sum_{m=1}^M\left(1-\operatorname{tr}(\Lambda_m\rho_{x^n(m)})\right).$$
Its rate is $n^{-1}\ln M$ nats per channel use, using the natural-log unit convention of [[def-it-von-neumann-entropy]]. A sequence of such codes is reliable if $e_n\to0$. The **classical capacity** $C_{\rm cq}$ is the supremum of $\liminf_{n\to\infty}n^{-1}\ln M_n$ over reliable sequences.

For each transmitted state, the POVM outcome weights sum to one by [[thm-qc-povm-probabilities-normalize]], so $e_n$ is the uniform-message block error probability.

Let $\mathcal N:A\to B$ be a finite-dimensional channel with chosen complement $\mathcal N^c:A\to E$, and let $\mathcal E=\{p_x,\rho_x\}_{x\in\mathcal X}$ be a finite ensemble on $A$ with $\bar\rho=\sum_xp_x\rho_x$. Then

$$I_p(\mathcal E,\mathcal N)=I_c(\bar\rho,\mathcal N)-\sum_{x:p_x>0}p_x I_c(\rho_x,\mathcal N).$$

definition_or_statement_use.text:
Let $\mathcal N:A\to B$ be a finite-dimensional quantum channel and use its memoryless extension $\mathcal N^{\otimes n}:A^{\otimes n}\to B^{\otimes n}$. Rates use natural logarithms, so they are in nats per channel use. For code sizes $K_n\ge1$, a rate $R\ge0$ is achievable when $\liminf_{n\to\infty}n^{-1}\ln K_n\ge R$ and the relevant error terms below tend to zero; each capacity is the supremum of its achievable rates.

For **quantum transmission**, a block code consists of an isometric encoder $W_n:M_n\to A^{\otimes n}$ and a quantum-channel decoder $\mathcal D_n:B^{\otimes n}\to M_n$, where $\dim M_n=K_n$. Let $R_n\cong M_n$ and let $|\Phi_{K_n}\rangle\in R_n\otimes M_n$ be a normalized maximally entangled vector. Its entanglement fidelity is

$$F_n:=\langle\Phi_{K_n}|(\operatorname{id}_{R_n}\otimes\mathcal D_n\mathcal N^{\otimes n}\mathcal W_n)(|\Phi_{K_n}\rangle\langle\Phi_{K_n}|)|\Phi_{K_n}\rangle,$$

where $\mathcal W_n(X)=W_nXW_n^*$. A rate is quantum-achievable if $F_n\to1$; the resulting capacity is $Q(\mathcal N)$. This is the subspace entanglement-transmission convention.

For **private classical transmission**, a block code uses equiprobable messages $m\in[K_n]$, input states $\rho_{m,n}$ on $A^{\otimes n}$, and a decoding POVM $\{\Lambda_{m,n}\}_{m=1}^{K_n}$ on $B^{\otimes n}$. Its average error is

$$e_n:=1-\frac1{K_n}\sum_{m=1}^{K_n}\operatorname{tr}(\Lambda_{m,n}\mathcal N^{\otimes n}(\rho_{m,n})).$$

Fix a complementary channel $\mathcal N^c$ as in [[def-it-quantum-channel-complement-and-coherent-information]]. Eve's average state is $\bar\tau_n=K_n^{-1}\sum_m(\mathcal N^c)^{\otimes n}(\rho_{m,n})$. Define leakage by its Holevo information

$$\ell_n:=S(\bar\tau_n)-\frac1{K_n}\sum_{m=1}^{K_n}S((\mathcal N^c)^{\otimes n}(\rho_{m,n})).$$

A rate is privately achievable when $e_n\to0$ and $\ell_n\to0$; this is strong secrecy in mutual-information form. The corresponding capacity is $P(\mathcal N)$. The value is independent of the chosen complementary dilation, as follows from [[lem-it-private-information-is-coherent-information-difference]].

For **classical transmission with prior shared entanglement**, for each block length $n$ the sender and receiver begin with a finite-dimensional shared state $\sigma_{S_AS_B}$ independent of the equiprobable message. For each $m\in[K_n]$, the sender applies a quantum channel $\mathcal E_{m,n}:\mathcal L(S_A)\to\mathcal L(A^{\otimes n})$. The receiver measures $B^{\otimes n}\otimes S_B$ with a POVM $\{\Gamma_{m,n}\}_{m=1}^{K_n}$. Its average error is

$$e_n^{EA}:=1-\frac1{K_n}\sum_{m=1}^{K_n}\operatorname{tr}\!\left[\Gamma_{m,n}\bigl((\mathcal N^{\otimes n}\circ\mathcal E_{m,n})\otimes\operatorname{id}_{S_B}\bigr)(\sigma_{S_AS_B})\right].$$ A rate is achievable when this error tends to zero; there is no constraint on the dimension or consumption of the shared entanglement. The resulting capacity is $C_E(\mathcal N)$.

The input, output, and reference registers are finite-dimensional in each block. No single-letter formula is included in these operational definitions.

Let $\rho$ be a density operator on a nonzero finite-dimensional source space, and use the squared entanglement-fidelity code model of [[def-it-quantum-source-and-compression-code]]. Write $S(\rho)$ in nats.

1. For every $R>S(\rho)$ there is a sequence of compression codes with $F_e^{(n)}\to1$ and $\limsup_n n^{-1}\ln M_n\le R$.
2. If a sequence of codes satisfies $\limsup_n n^{-1}\ln M_n<S(\rho)$, then $F_e^{(n)}\to0$.

Thus the asymptotic reliable compression rate is exactly $S(\rho)$ nats per source letter, or $S(\rho)/\ln2$ qubits per source letter.

Let $X$ be a finite nonempty classical label set, represented by a register $H_X$ with computational orthonormal basis $(\xi_x)_{x\in X}$ ([[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]]). For each $x$, write $\Pi_xz:=\langle z,\xi_x\rangle\xi_x$, the rank-one orthogonal projection using the root linear-first convention, as in [[lem-it-finite-cq-block-sum-is-a-state]]. Let $H_B$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space. A finite **classical-quantum state** is

$$\rho_{XB}:=\sum_{x\in X}p_x\Pi_x\otimes\rho_x,$$

where $p_x\ge0$, $\sum_xp_x=1$, and each $\rho_x$ is a density operator on $H_B$. It is a density operator by [[lem-it-finite-cq-block-sum-is-a-state]]. Its quantum marginal is $\bar\rho_B:=\sum_xp_x\rho_x=\operatorname{Tr}_X\rho_{XB}$ by the second-factor partial-trace formula in [[def-qc-partial-trace]], and it is a density operator by [[lem-it-partial-traces-of-a-state-are-states]]. The **Holevo information** of this ensemble is

$$\chi(\{p_x,\rho_x\}_{x\in X}):=S(\bar\rho_B)-\sum_{x:p_x>0}p_xS(\rho_x),$$

where zero-probability branches contribute nothing. This is measured in nats under [[def-it-von-neumann-entropy]].

The coordinate indicators are independent under $p^{\otimes n}$ and have variance at most $1/4$; [F6]–[F9] give $p^{\otimes n}(T_n^c)\le|\mathcal X|/(4n\kappa^2)\to0$. For each $x$ with $p_x>0$, $\bar\sigma\succeq p_x\sigma_x$ by [F3] and [F10]; a vector in $\ker\bar\sigma$ therefore has zero quadratic form for $\sigma_x$, so [F5] gives $\operatorname{supp}\sigma_x\subseteq\operatorname{supp}\bar\sigma$. The spectral logarithm on the latter positive support is bounded in finite dimension by [F4], making $\mu_x:=\operatorname{tr}(\sigma_x[-\ln\bar\sigma])$ finite for every such $x$. Define this family only for $p_x>0$; the zero-probability symbols never occur in $T_n$. Choose $\kappa>0$ small enough that the empirical averages of each of the two finite families $S(\sigma_x)$ and $\mu_x$, restricted to $p_x>0$, differ from their $p$-averages by at most $\delta/2$ on $T_n$. These choices are possible because both restricted families are finite and their entries are finite. [F3, F4, F5, F6, F8, F9, F10, given, choose]

For a finite bipartite state $\rho_{AB}$ on the ordered product $H_A\otimes H_B$, write $\rho_A=\operatorname{Tr}_B\rho_{AB}$ and $\rho_B=\operatorname{Tr}_A\rho_{AB}$, using the partial traces in [[def-qc-partial-trace]] and [[def-qc-first-factor-partial-trace]]. They are states by [[lem-it-partial-traces-of-a-state-are-states]]. Define

$$S(A)_\rho:=S(\rho_A),\qquad S(A\mid B)_\rho:=S(\rho_{AB})-S(\rho_B),\qquad I(A:B)_\rho:=S(\rho_A)+S(\rho_B)-S(\rho_{AB}).$$

For a finite tripartite state $\rho_{ABC}$ on the ordered product $H_A\otimes H_B\otimes H_C$, set $\rho_{AB}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_C}\rho_{ABC}$ after identifying the factors as $(H_A\otimes H_B)\otimes H_C$, and $\rho_{BC}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_A}\rho_{ABC}$ after identifying them as $H_A\otimes(H_B\otimes H_C)$. Let $P:H_A\otimes H_B\otimes H_C\to H_A\otimes H_C\otimes H_B$ be the wire permutation taking factor order $A,B,C$ to $A,C,B$ ([[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]], [[thm-qc-wire-permutation-is-unitary]]) whose unique adjoint $P^*$ exists by [[thm-adjoint-exists-and-is-unique-in-finite-dimension]], and set $\rho_{AC}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_B}(P\rho_{ABC}P^*)$, tracing out the last factor. Because $P$ is unitary, $P\rho_{ABC}P^*$ is a state: unitary conjugation preserves non-negativity by the adjoint identity ([[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]], [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]) and preserves trace by cyclicity ([[thm-trace-of-ab-equals-trace-of-ba]]). Finally set $\rho_C:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_B}\rho_{BC}$. All these marginals are density operators by applying [[lem-it-partial-traces-of-a-state-are-states]] after grouping factors. Define

$$I(A:B\mid C)_\rho:=S(\rho_{AC})+S(\rho_{BC})-S(\rho_C)-S(\rho_{ABC}).$$

These are finite-dimensional definitions only; no non-negativity of conditional entropy or conditional mutual information is part of the notation.

They are states by [[lem-it-partial-traces-of-a-state-are-states]]. Define

$$S(A)_\rho:=S(\rho_A),\qquad S(A\mid B)_\rho:=S(\rho_{AB})-S(\rho_B),\qquad I(A:B)_\rho:=S(\rho_A)+S(\rho_B)-S(\rho_{AB}).$$

For a finite tripartite state $\rho_{ABC}$ on the ordered product $H_A\otimes H_B\otimes H_C$, set $\rho_{AB}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_C}\rho_{ABC}$ after identifying the factors as $(H_A\otimes H_B)\otimes H_C$, and $\rho_{BC}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_A}\rho_{ABC}$ after identifying them as $H_A\otimes(H_B\otimes H_C)$. Let $P:H_A\otimes H_B\otimes H_C\to H_A\otimes H_C\otimes H_B$ be the wire permutation taking factor order $A,B,C$ to $A,C,B$ ([[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]], [[thm-qc-wire-permutation-is-unitary]]) whose unique adjoint $P^*$ exists by [[thm-adjoint-exists-and-is-unique-in-finite-dimension]], and set $\rho_{AC}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_B}(P\rho_{ABC}P^*)$, tracing out the last factor. Because $P$ is unitary, $P\rho_{ABC}P^*$ is a state: unitary conjugation preserves non-negativity by the adjoint identity ([[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]], [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]) and preserves trace by cyclicity ([[thm-trace-of-ab-equals-trace-of-ba]]). $$I(A:B\mid C)_\rho:=S(\rho_{AC})+S(\rho_{BC})-S(\rho_C)-S(\rho_{ABC}).$$

For every fixed finite ensemble $p_x,\rho_x$ and fixed $\eta>0$, there are constants $C,c>0$ (depending on this ensemble and $\eta$, not $n$) and projectors $P_n,Q_{x^n}$ such that, writing $\bar\rho=\sum p_x\rho_x$ and $s=\sum p_xS(\rho_x)$,
$$\operatorname{rank}P_n\le e^{n(S(\bar\rho)+\eta)},\quad P_n\bar\rho^{\otimes n}P_n\preceq e^{-n(S(\bar\rho)-\eta)}P_n,$$
$$\operatorname{rank}Q_{x^n}\le e^{n(s+\eta)},\quad Q_{x^n}\rho_{x^n}Q_{x^n}\preceq e^{-n(s-\eta)}Q_{x^n},$$
and
$$\mathbb E\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{X^n}(I-P_n))\le Ce^{-cn},\qquad\mathbb E\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{X^n}(I-Q_{X^n}))\le Ce^{-cn}.$$
The second pair of algebraic bounds holds for every word, including words with zero sampling probability; no per-word high-acceptance assertion is required.

For density operators $\rho,\sigma$ on a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space,

$$D(\rho\|\sigma)\ge0,$$

with equality if and only if $\rho=\sigma$.

exact_consumer_facts: [F2] [[thm-it-quantum-relative-entropy-nonnegative-equality]]: Nonnegativity and equality for finite quantum relative entropy.
actual_proof_uses: 1.1 Omit zero weights. For each $i$ with $p_i>0$, $\bar\rho-p_i\rho_i=\sum_{j\ne i}p_j\rho_j$ is non-negative. If $v\in\ker\bar\rho$, its quadratic form under this sum is zero; every summand is nonnegative, so $\langle\rho_i v,v\rangle=0$ and [F5] gives $\rho_i v=0$. Hence $\operatorname{supp}\rho_i\subseteq\operatorname{supp}\bar\rho$ and every $D(\rho_i\|\bar\rho)$ is finite. The trace formula [F6], linearity of trace [F4], and $\bar\rho=\sum_i p_i\rho_i$ give $$\sum_i p_iD(\rho_i\Vert\bar\rho)=S(\bar\rho)-\sum_i p_iS(\rho_i)\ge0$$ by [F2]. [F1, F2, F4, F5, F6, given, algebra, construct]

2.1 For the upper bound, diagonalize each $\rho_i=\sum_j\lambda_{ij}|v_{ij}\rangle\langle v_{ij}|$, omitting zero weights and eigenvalues, and purify the mixture as $|v\rangle=\sum_{ij}\sqrt{p_i\lambda_{ij}}|v_{ij}\rangle\otimes|i,j\rangle$. Its label marginal $G$ has diagonal $q_{ij}=p_i\lambda_{ij}$ and has the same nonzero eigenvalues as $\bar\rho$ by Schmidt decomposition. The logarithm product law in [F6] gives $H(q)=H(p)+\sum_i p_iS(\rho_i)$. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F6, given, algebra, construct, step 1.1]

3.1 For $\Delta=\operatorname{diag}(q)$, if $v\in\ker\Delta$, then $\langle Gv,v\rangle=0$ because $G$ is non-negative and has diagonal $q$; [F5] gives $Gv=0$. Thus $\operatorname{supp}G\subseteq\operatorname{supp}\Delta$. The formula [F6] now gives $$0\le D(G\Vert\Delta)=H(q)-S(G)=H(p)+\sum_i p_iS(\rho_i)-S(\bar\rho).$$ This proves both bounds, including singleton/zero-weight cases. Let $X$ be a finite nonempty classical label set, represented by a register $H_X$ with computational orthonormal basis $(\xi_x)_{x\in X}$ ([[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]]). For each $x$, write $\Pi_xz:=\langle z,\xi_x\rangle\xi_x$, the rank-one orthogonal projection using the root linear-first convention, as in [[lem-it-finite-cq-block-sum-is-a-state]]. Let $H_B$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space. A finite **classical-quantum state** is

$$\rho_{XB}:=\sum_{x\in X}p_x\Pi_x\otimes\rho_x,$$

where $p_x\ge0$, $\sum_xp_x=1$, and each $\rho_x$ is a density operator on $H_B$. It is a density operator by [[lem-it-finite-cq-block-sum-is-a-state]]. Its quantum marginal is $\bar\rho_B:=\sum_xp_x\rho_x=\operatorname{Tr}_X\rho_{XB}$ by the second-factor partial-trace formula in [[def-qc-partial-trace]], and it is a density operator by [[lem-it-partial-traces-of-a-state-are-states]]. The **Holevo information** of this ensemble is

$$\chi(\{p_x,\rho_x\}_{x\in X}):=S(\bar\rho_B)-\sum_{x:p_x>0}p_xS(\rho_x),$$

where zero-probability branches contribute nothing. This is measured in nats under [[def-it-von-neumann-entropy]].

Their average is $\mathcal N(\tau)\otimes I_R/D$. Its collective POVM is a permitted receiver measurement and its rate/error are exactly those of HSW. $$C_{\rm cq}=\max_{p\in\Delta(\mathcal X)}\chi_p,\qquad \chi_p:=S\!\left(\sum_xp_x\rho_x\right)-\sum_{x:p_x>0}p_xS(\rho_x).$$

Let $\mathcal N:A\to B$ be a finite-dimensional quantum channel and use its memoryless extension $\mathcal N^{\otimes n}:A^{\otimes n}\to B^{\otimes n}$. Rates use natural logarithms, so they are in nats per channel use. For code sizes $K_n\ge1$, a rate $R\ge0$ is achievable when $\liminf_{n\to\infty}n^{-1}\ln K_n\ge R$ and the relevant error terms below tend to zero; each capacity is the supremum of its achievable rates.

For **quantum transmission**, a block code consists of an isometric encoder $W_n:M_n\to A^{\otimes n}$ and a quantum-channel decoder $\mathcal D_n:B^{\otimes n}\to M_n$, where $\dim M_n=K_n$. Let $R_n\cong M_n$ and let $|\Phi_{K_n}\rangle\in R_n\otimes M_n$ be a normalized maximally entangled vector. Its entanglement fidelity is

$$F_n:=\langle\Phi_{K_n}|(\operatorname{id}_{R_n}\otimes\mathcal D_n\mathcal N^{\otimes n}\mathcal W_n)(|\Phi_{K_n}\rangle\langle\Phi_{K_n}|)|\Phi_{K_n}\rangle,$$

where $\mathcal W_n(X)=W_nXW_n^*$. A rate is quantum-achievable if $F_n\to1$; the resulting capacity is $Q(\mathcal N)$. This is the subspace entanglement-transmission convention.

For **private classical transmission**, a block code uses equiprobable messages $m\in[K_n]$, input states $\rho_{m,n}$ on $A^{\otimes n}$, and a decoding POVM $\{\Lambda_{m,n}\}_{m=1}^{K_n}$ on $B^{\otimes n}$. Its average error is

$$e_n:=1-\frac1{K_n}\sum_{m=1}^{K_n}\operatorname{tr}(\Lambda_{m,n}\mathcal N^{\otimes n}(\rho_{m,n})).$$

Fix a complementary channel $\mathcal N^c$ as in [[def-it-quantum-channel-complement-and-coherent-information]]. Eve's average state is $\bar\tau_n=K_n^{-1}\sum_m(\mathcal N^c)^{\otimes n}(\rho_{m,n})$. Define leakage by its Holevo information

$$\ell_n:=S(\bar\tau_n)-\frac1{K_n}\sum_{m=1}^{K_n}S((\mathcal N^c)^{\otimes n}(\rho_{m,n})).$$

A rate is privately achievable when $e_n\to0$ and $\ell_n\to0$; this is strong secrecy in mutual-information form. The corresponding capacity is $P(\mathcal N)$. The value is independent of the chosen complementary dilation, as follows from [[lem-it-private-information-is-coherent-information-difference]].

For **classical transmission with prior shared entanglement**, for each block length $n$ the sender and receiver begin with a finite-dimensional shared state $\sigma_{S_AS_B}$ independent of the equiprobable message. For each $m\in[K_n]$, the sender applies a quantum channel $\mathcal E_{m,n}:\mathcal L(S_A)\to\mathcal L(A^{\otimes n})$. The receiver measures $B^{\otimes n}\otimes S_B$ with a POVM $\{\Gamma_{m,n}\}_{m=1}^{K_n}$. Its average error is

$$e_n^{EA}:=1-\frac1{K_n}\sum_{m=1}^{K_n}\operatorname{tr}\!\left[\Gamma_{m,n}\bigl((\mathcal N^{\otimes n}\circ\mathcal E_{m,n})\otimes\operatorname{id}_{S_B}\bigr)(\sigma_{S_AS_B})\right].$$ A rate is achievable when this error tends to zero; there is no constraint on the dimension or consumption of the shared entanglement. $$I_c(\rho_{A_1A_2},\mathcal N_1\otimes\mathcal N_2)\le I_c(\rho_{A_1},\mathcal N_1)+I_c(\rho_{A_2},\mathcal N_2).$$

Let $X$ be a finite nonempty set, let $(p_x)$ be a probability vector, let $\rho_x$ be density operators on a nonzero finite-dimensional space $H_B$, and let $\bar\rho:=\sum_xp_x\rho_x$. $$I(X:Y):=\sum_{x,y:p_xw(y\mid x)>0}p_xw(y\mid x)\ln\frac{w(y\mid x)}{q_y}.$$

Then

$$I(X:Y)\le\chi(\{p_x,\rho_x\})=S(\bar\rho)-\sum_{x:p_x>0}p_xS(\rho_x).$$

Let $x\mapsto\rho_x$ be a finite-input, finite-output memoryless cq channel as in [[def-it-classical-quantum-memoryless-channel]]. With the average-error code convention of [[def-it-cq-channel-block-code-and-error]], its classical capacity in nats per use is
$$C_{\rm cq}=\max_{p\in\Delta(\mathcal X)}\chi_p,\qquad \chi_p:=S\!\left(\sum_xp_x\rho_x\right)-\sum_{x:p_x>0}p_xS(\rho_x).$$
For every $0\le R<C_{\rm cq}$ a sequence of codes with rate tending to $R$ has average error tending to zero, and every reliable sequence has limiting upper rate at most $C_{\rm cq}$. This theorem concerns a fixed finite classical input alphabet and does not assert a single-letter formula for general quantum-input channels.

Let $\rho$ be a density operator on a nonzero finite-dimensional source space, and use the squared entanglement-fidelity code model of [[def-it-quantum-source-and-compression-code]]. Write $S(\rho)$ in nats.

1. For every $R>S(\rho)$ there is a sequence of compression codes with $F_e^{(n)}\to1$ and $\limsup_n n^{-1}\ln M_n\le R$.
2. If a sequence of codes satisfies $\limsup_n n^{-1}\ln M_n<S(\rho)$, then $F_e^{(n)}\to0$.

Thus the asymptotic reliable compression rate is exactly $S(\rho)$ nats per source letter, or $S(\rho)/\ln2$ qubits per source letter.

For a finite bipartite state $\rho_{AB}$ on the ordered product $H_A\otimes H_B$, write $\rho_A=\operatorname{Tr}_B\rho_{AB}$ and $\rho_B=\operatorname{Tr}_A\rho_{AB}$, using the partial traces in [[def-qc-partial-trace]] and [[def-qc-first-factor-partial-trace]]. They are states by [[lem-it-partial-traces-of-a-state-are-states]]. Define

$$S(A)_\rho:=S(\rho_A),\qquad S(A\mid B)_\rho:=S(\rho_{AB})-S(\rho_B),\qquad I(A:B)_\rho:=S(\rho_A)+S(\rho_B)-S(\rho_{AB}).$$

For a finite tripartite state $\rho_{ABC}$ on the ordered product $H_A\otimes H_B\otimes H_C$, set $\rho_{AB}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_C}\rho_{ABC}$ after identifying the factors as $(H_A\otimes H_B)\otimes H_C$, and $\rho_{BC}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_A}\rho_{ABC}$ after identifying them as $H_A\otimes(H_B\otimes H_C)$. Let $P:H_A\otimes H_B\otimes H_C\to H_A\otimes H_C\otimes H_B$ be the wire permutation taking factor order $A,B,C$ to $A,C,B$ ([[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]], [[thm-qc-wire-permutation-is-unitary]]) whose unique adjoint $P^*$ exists by [[thm-adjoint-exists-and-is-unique-in-finite-dimension]], and set $\rho_{AC}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_B}(P\rho_{ABC}P^*)$, tracing out the last factor. Because $P$ is unitary, $P\rho_{ABC}P^*$ is a state: unitary conjugation preserves non-negativity by the adjoint identity ([[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]], [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]) and preserves trace by cyclicity ([[thm-trace-of-ab-equals-trace-of-ba]]). Finally set $\rho_C:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_B}\rho_{BC}$. All these marginals are density operators by applying [[lem-it-partial-traces-of-a-state-are-states]] after grouping factors. Define

$$I(A:B\mid C)_\rho:=S(\rho_{AC})+S(\rho_{BC})-S(\rho_C)-S(\rho_{ABC}).$$

These are finite-dimensional definitions only; no non-negativity of conditional entropy or conditional mutual information is part of the notation.

Let $X$ be a finite nonempty classical label set, represented by a register $H_X$ with computational orthonormal basis $(\xi_x)_{x\in X}$ ([[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]]). For each $x$, write $\Pi_xz:=\langle z,\xi_x\rangle\xi_x$, the rank-one orthogonal projection using the root linear-first convention, as in [[lem-it-finite-cq-block-sum-is-a-state]]. Let $H_B$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space. A finite **classical-quantum state** is

$$\rho_{XB}:=\sum_{x\in X}p_x\Pi_x\otimes\rho_x,$$

where $p_x\ge0$, $\sum_xp_x=1$, and each $\rho_x$ is a density operator on $H_B$. It is a density operator by [[lem-it-finite-cq-block-sum-is-a-state]]. Its quantum marginal is $\bar\rho_B:=\sum_xp_x\rho_x=\operatorname{Tr}_X\rho_{XB}$ by the second-factor partial-trace formula in [[def-qc-partial-trace]], and it is a density operator by [[lem-it-partial-traces-of-a-state-are-states]]. The **Holevo information** of this ensemble is

$$\chi(\{p_x,\rho_x\}_{x\in X}):=S(\bar\rho_B)-\sum_{x:p_x>0}p_xS(\rho_x),$$

where zero-probability branches contribute nothing. This is measured in nats under [[def-it-von-neumann-entropy]].

Let $\mathcal X$ be a finite nonempty input alphabet and let $H_B$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space. A **finite-input cq channel** is a map $x\mapsto\rho_x$ assigning a density operator ([[def-qc-density-operator]]) $\rho_x$ on $H_B$ to each $x\in\mathcal X$. Its $n$-use memoryless extension sends a word $x^n=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$ to the product state
$$\rho_{x^n}:=\rho_{x_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes\rho_{x_n}\quad\text{on }H_B^{\otimes n}.$$
For an input probability vector $p$, write $\bar\rho_p=\sum_xp_x\rho_x$ and $\chi_p=S(\bar\rho_p)-\sum_{x:p_x>0}p_xS(\rho_x)$; this is the Holevo information of the ensemble in [[def-it-classical-quantum-state-and-holevo-information]], in nats.

Let $x\mapsto\rho_x$ be a finite-input, finite-output memoryless cq channel as in [[def-it-classical-quantum-memoryless-channel]]. With the average-error code convention of [[def-it-cq-channel-block-code-and-error]], its classical capacity in nats per use is
$$C_{\rm cq}=\max_{p\in\Delta(\mathcal X)}\chi_p,\qquad \chi_p:=S\!\left(\sum_xp_x\rho_x\right)-\sum_{x:p_x>0}p_xS(\rho_x).$$
For every $0\le R<C_{\rm cq}$ a sequence of codes with rate tending to $R$ has average error tending to zero, and every reliable sequence has limiting upper rate at most $C_{\rm cq}$. This theorem concerns a fixed finite classical input alphabet and does not assert a single-letter formula for general quantum-input channels.

exact_supplier_export.text:
Fix a finite-input cq channel as in [[def-it-classical-quantum-memoryless-channel]]. For integers $n,M\ge1$, an $(n,M)$ **cq block code** consists of a deterministic encoder $m\mapsto x^n(m)\in\mathcal X^n$ for $m\in[M]:=\{1,\ldots,M\}$ and a finite POVM ([[def-qc-povm-and-outcome-law]]) $(\Lambda_m)_{m\in[M]}$ on $H_B^{\otimes n}$. Under a uniform message, its **average block error** is
$$e_n:=\frac1M\sum_{m=1}^M\left(1-\operatorname{tr}(\Lambda_m\rho_{x^n(m)})\right).$$
Its rate is $n^{-1}\ln M$ nats per channel use, using the natural-log unit convention of [[def-it-von-neumann-entropy]]. A sequence of such codes is reliable if $e_n\to0$. The **classical capacity** $C_{\rm cq}$ is the supremum of $\liminf_{n\to\infty}n^{-1}\ln M_n$ over reliable sequences.

For each transmitted state, the POVM outcome weights sum to one by [[thm-qc-povm-probabilities-normalize]], so $e_n$ is the uniform-message block error probability.

All logarithms are natural. First, for every density operator $\rho$ on a nonzero finite-dimensional space and every $\delta>0$, there are spectral projectors $\Pi_n$ for $\rho^{\otimes n}$ such that, as $n\to\infty$,
$$\operatorname{tr}(\Pi_n\rho^{\otimes n})\to1,\qquad \operatorname{rank}\Pi_n\le e^{n(S(\rho)+\delta)},\qquad \Pi_n\rho^{\otimes n}\Pi_n\preceq e^{-n(S(\rho)-\delta)}\Pi_n.$$

Second, let $\mathcal X$ be a finite nonempty set, let $(p_x)_{x\in\mathcal X}$ be a probability vector, and let $\sigma_x$ be density operators on a nonzero finite-dimensional output space. Put $\bar\sigma=\sum_xp_x\sigma_x$ and $H(B|X)=\sum_{x:p_x>0}p_xS(\sigma_x)$. For every $\delta>0$, there are sets $T_n\subseteq\mathcal X^n$ with $p^{\otimes n}(T_n)\to1$, global spectral projectors $\Pi_n$ for $\bar\sigma^{\otimes n}$, and conditional spectral projectors $\Pi_{x^n}$ for $\bigotimes_i\sigma_{x_i}$, such that one sequence $u_n\to0$ satisfies, for every sufficiently large $n$ and every $x^n\in T_n$,
$$\operatorname{tr}(\Pi_n\bar\sigma^{\otimes n})\to1,\quad \operatorname{tr}(\Pi_n\bigotimes_i\sigma_{x_i})\ge1-u_n,\quad \operatorname{tr}(\Pi_{x^n}\bigotimes_i\sigma_{x_i})\ge1-u_n,$$
$$\operatorname{rank}\Pi_n\le e^{n(S(\bar\sigma)+\delta)},\quad \Pi_n\bar\sigma^{\otimes n}\Pi_n\preceq e^{-n(S(\bar\sigma)-\delta)}\Pi_n,$$
$$\operatorname{rank}\Pi_{x^n}\le e^{n(H(B|X)+\delta)},\quad \Pi_{x^n}\left(\bigotimes_i\sigma_{x_i}\right)\Pi_{x^n}\preceq e^{-n(H(B|X)-\delta)}\Pi_{x^n}.$$

Let $\mathcal N:A\to B$ be a finite-dimensional quantum channel and use its memoryless extension $\mathcal N^{\otimes n}:A^{\otimes n}\to B^{\otimes n}$. Rates use natural logarithms, so they are in nats per channel use. For code sizes $K_n\ge1$, a rate $R\ge0$ is achievable when $\liminf_{n\to\infty}n^{-1}\ln K_n\ge R$ and the relevant error terms below tend to zero; each capacity is the supremum of its achievable rates.

For **quantum transmission**, a block code consists of an isometric encoder $W_n:M_n\to A^{\otimes n}$ and a quantum-channel decoder $\mathcal D_n:B^{\otimes n}\to M_n$, where $\dim M_n=K_n$. Let $R_n\cong M_n$ and let $|\Phi_{K_n}\rangle\in R_n\otimes M_n$ be a normalized maximally entangled vector. Its entanglement fidelity is

$$F_n:=\langle\Phi_{K_n}|(\operatorname{id}_{R_n}\otimes\mathcal D_n\mathcal N^{\otimes n}\mathcal W_n)(|\Phi_{K_n}\rangle\langle\Phi_{K_n}|)|\Phi_{K_n}\rangle,$$

where $\mathcal W_n(X)=W_nXW_n^*$. A rate is quantum-achievable if $F_n\to1$; the resulting capacity is $Q(\mathcal N)$. This is the subspace entanglement-transmission convention.

For **private classical transmission**, a block code uses equiprobable messages $m\in[K_n]$, input states $\rho_{m,n}$ on $A^{\otimes n}$, and a decoding POVM $\{\Lambda_{m,n}\}_{m=1}^{K_n}$ on $B^{\otimes n}$. Its average error is

$$e_n:=1-\frac1{K_n}\sum_{m=1}^{K_n}\operatorname{tr}(\Lambda_{m,n}\mathcal N^{\otimes n}(\rho_{m,n})).$$

Fix a complementary channel $\mathcal N^c$ as in [[def-it-quantum-channel-complement-and-coherent-information]]. Eve's average state is $\bar\tau_n=K_n^{-1}\sum_m(\mathcal N^c)^{\otimes n}(\rho_{m,n})$. Define leakage by its Holevo information

$$\ell_n:=S(\bar\tau_n)-\frac1{K_n}\sum_{m=1}^{K_n}S((\mathcal N^c)^{\otimes n}(\rho_{m,n})).$$

A rate is privately achievable when $e_n\to0$ and $\ell_n\to0$; this is strong secrecy in mutual-information form. The corresponding capacity is $P(\mathcal N)$. The value is independent of the chosen complementary dilation, as follows from [[lem-it-private-information-is-coherent-information-difference]].

For **classical transmission with prior shared entanglement**, for each block length $n$ the sender and receiver begin with a finite-dimensional shared state $\sigma_{S_AS_B}$ independent of the equiprobable message. For each $m\in[K_n]$, the sender applies a quantum channel $\mathcal E_{m,n}:\mathcal L(S_A)\to\mathcal L(A^{\otimes n})$. The receiver measures $B^{\otimes n}\otimes S_B$ with a POVM $\{\Gamma_{m,n}\}_{m=1}^{K_n}$. Its average error is

$$e_n^{EA}:=1-\frac1{K_n}\sum_{m=1}^{K_n}\operatorname{tr}\!\left[\Gamma_{m,n}\bigl((\mathcal N^{\otimes n}\circ\mathcal E_{m,n})\otimes\operatorname{id}_{S_B}\bigr)(\sigma_{S_AS_B})\right].$$ A rate is achievable when this error tends to zero; there is no constraint on the dimension or consumption of the shared entanglement. The resulting capacity is $C_E(\mathcal N)$.

The input, output, and reference registers are finite-dimensional in each block. No single-letter formula is included in these operational definitions.

Let $\mathcal N:A\to B$ be a finite-dimensional quantum channel and use its memoryless extension $\mathcal N^{\otimes n}:A^{\otimes n}\to B^{\otimes n}$. Rates use natural logarithms, so they are in nats per channel use. For code sizes $K_n\ge1$, a rate $R\ge0$ is achievable when $\liminf_{n\to\infty}n^{-1}\ln K_n\ge R$ and the relevant error terms below tend to zero; each capacity is the supremum of its achievable rates.

For **quantum transmission**, a block code consists of an isometric encoder $W_n:M_n\to A^{\otimes n}$ and a quantum-channel decoder $\mathcal D_n:B^{\otimes n}\to M_n$, where $\dim M_n=K_n$. Let $R_n\cong M_n$ and let $|\Phi_{K_n}\rangle\in R_n\otimes M_n$ be a normalized maximally entangled vector. Its entanglement fidelity is

$$F_n:=\langle\Phi_{K_n}|(\operatorname{id}_{R_n}\otimes\mathcal D_n\mathcal N^{\otimes n}\mathcal W_n)(|\Phi_{K_n}\rangle\langle\Phi_{K_n}|)|\Phi_{K_n}\rangle,$$

where $\mathcal W_n(X)=W_nXW_n^*$. A rate is quantum-achievable if $F_n\to1$; the resulting capacity is $Q(\mathcal N)$. This is the subspace entanglement-transmission convention.

For **private classical transmission**, a block code uses equiprobable messages $m\in[K_n]$, input states $\rho_{m,n}$ on $A^{\otimes n}$, and a decoding POVM $\{\Lambda_{m,n}\}_{m=1}^{K_n}$ on $B^{\otimes n}$. Its average error is

$$e_n:=1-\frac1{K_n}\sum_{m=1}^{K_n}\operatorname{tr}(\Lambda_{m,n}\mathcal N^{\otimes n}(\rho_{m,n})).$$

Fix a complementary channel $\mathcal N^c$ as in [[def-it-quantum-channel-complement-and-coherent-information]]. Eve's average state is $\bar\tau_n=K_n^{-1}\sum_m(\mathcal N^c)^{\otimes n}(\rho_{m,n})$. Define leakage by its Holevo information

$$\ell_n:=S(\bar\tau_n)-\frac1{K_n}\sum_{m=1}^{K_n}S((\mathcal N^c)^{\otimes n}(\rho_{m,n})).$$

A rate is privately achievable when $e_n\to0$ and $\ell_n\to0$; this is strong secrecy in mutual-information form. The corresponding capacity is $P(\mathcal N)$. The value is independent of the chosen complementary dilation, as follows from [[lem-it-private-information-is-coherent-information-difference]].

For **classical transmission with prior shared entanglement**, for each block length $n$ the sender and receiver begin with a finite-dimensional shared state $\sigma_{S_AS_B}$ independent of the equiprobable message. For each $m\in[K_n]$, the sender applies a quantum channel $\mathcal E_{m,n}:\mathcal L(S_A)\to\mathcal L(A^{\otimes n})$. The receiver measures $B^{\otimes n}\otimes S_B$ with a POVM $\{\Gamma_{m,n}\}_{m=1}^{K_n}$. Its average error is

$$e_n^{EA}:=1-\frac1{K_n}\sum_{m=1}^{K_n}\operatorname{tr}\!\left[\Gamma_{m,n}\bigl((\mathcal N^{\otimes n}\circ\mathcal E_{m,n})\otimes\operatorname{id}_{S_B}\bigr)(\sigma_{S_AS_B})\right].$$ A rate is achievable when this error tends to zero; there is no constraint on the dimension or consumption of the shared entanglement. The resulting capacity is $C_E(\mathcal N)$.

The input, output, and reference registers are finite-dimensional in each block. No single-letter formula is included in these operational definitions.

$$I(A:B)_\rho=S(\rho_A)+S(\rho_B)-S(\rho_{AB})=D(\rho_{AB}\|\rho_A\otimes\rho_B).$$

For a finite classical-quantum state $\rho_{XB}=\sum_xp_x\Pi_x\otimes\rho_x$, its mutual information equals its Holevo information:

$$I(X:B)_\rho=S\!\left(\sum_xp_x\rho_x\right)-\sum_{x:p_x>0}p_xS(\rho_x)=\chi(\{p_x,\rho_x\}).$$

exact_consumer_facts: [F2] [[def-it-finite-quantum-information-measures]] and [[thm-it-quantum-entropy-identities]]: for a finite classical-quantum state, $I(X;B)$ is its Holevo information.
actual_proof_uses: 1.1 Write $p_n=p_n(\mathcal N)$. The one-state ensemble has private information zero, so $p_n\ge0$. For any finite ensemble, [F1]–[F3] give $I_p=I(X;B^n)-I(X;E^n)\le I(X;B^n)$, since [F3] implies $I(X;E^n)\ge0$. By [F2] and [F7], $I(X;B^n)=S(B^n)-\sum_xp_xS(B_x)\le S(B^n)$ because each conditional output entropy is nonnegative by [F6]. The output dimension and logarithm identity in [F8], together with [F6], give $S(B^n)\le n\ln\dim B$. Therefore $0\le p_n\le n\ln\dim B$. [F1, F2, F3, F6, F7, F8, given, algebra]

Let $X$ be a finite nonempty classical label set, represented by a register $H_X$ with computational orthonormal basis $(\xi_x)_{x\in X}$ ([[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]]). For each $x$, write $\Pi_xz:=\langle z,\xi_x\rangle\xi_x$, the rank-one orthogonal projection using the root linear-first convention, as in [[lem-it-finite-cq-block-sum-is-a-state]]. Let $H_B$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space. A finite **classical-quantum state** is

$$\rho_{XB}:=\sum_{x\in X}p_x\Pi_x\otimes\rho_x,$$

where $p_x\ge0$, $\sum_xp_x=1$, and each $\rho_x$ is a density operator on $H_B$. It is a density operator by [[lem-it-finite-cq-block-sum-is-a-state]]. Its quantum marginal is $\bar\rho_B:=\sum_xp_x\rho_x=\operatorname{Tr}_X\rho_{XB}$ by the second-factor partial-trace formula in [[def-qc-partial-trace]], and it is a density operator by [[lem-it-partial-traces-of-a-state-are-states]]. The **Holevo information** of this ensemble is

$$\chi(\{p_x,\rho_x\}_{x\in X}):=S(\bar\rho_B)-\sum_{x:p_x>0}p_xS(\rho_x),$$

where zero-probability branches contribute nothing. This is measured in nats under [[def-it-von-neumann-entropy]].

exact_consumer_facts: [F4] [[def-it-classical-quantum-state-and-holevo-information]]: $\rho_{XB}=\sum_xp_x\Pi_x\otimes\rho_x$, $\rho_B=\sum_xp_x\rho_x$, and $\chi=S(\rho_B)-\sum_{p_x>0}p_xS(\rho_x)$.
actual_proof_uses: 4.1 In the orthogonal blocks of $\rho_{XB}$, the eigenvalues are $p_x\lambda_{xj}$, where $\lambda_{xj}$ are the eigenvalues of $\rho_x$; zero-probability blocks contribute only zeros. By [F7] and $\operatorname{tr}ρ_x=1$, $\rho_X=\sum_xp_x\Pi_x$; its eigenvalues are $(p_x)$, and the $B$-marginal is $\bar\rho_B=\sum_xp_x\rho_x$ by [F4]. The block eigenvalues follow from [F9]. Expanding $-(p_x\lambda_{xj})\ln(p_x\lambda_{xj})$ and using $\sum_j\lambda_{xj}=1$ gives $S(\rho_{XB})=S(\rho_X)+\sum_{x:p_x>0}p_xS(\rho_x)$ by [F10]. Substitution into the definition [F1] cancels $S(\rho_X)$ and proves $I(X:B)_\rho=\chi(\{p_x,\rho_x\})$. [given, F1, F4, F7, F9, F10, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

For a finite bipartite state $\rho_{AB}$ on the ordered product $H_A\otimes H_B$, write $\rho_A=\operatorname{Tr}_B\rho_{AB}$ and $\rho_B=\operatorname{Tr}_A\rho_{AB}$, using the partial traces in [[def-qc-partial-trace]] and [[def-qc-first-factor-partial-trace]]. They are states by [[lem-it-partial-traces-of-a-state-are-states]]. Define

$$S(A)_\rho:=S(\rho_A),\qquad S(A\mid B)_\rho:=S(\rho_{AB})-S(\rho_B),\qquad I(A:B)_\rho:=S(\rho_A)+S(\rho_B)-S(\rho_{AB}).$$

For a finite tripartite state $\rho_{ABC}$ on the ordered product $H_A\otimes H_B\otimes H_C$, set $\rho_{AB}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_C}\rho_{ABC}$ after identifying the factors as $(H_A\otimes H_B)\otimes H_C$, and $\rho_{BC}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_A}\rho_{ABC}$ after identifying them as $H_A\otimes(H_B\otimes H_C)$. Let $P:H_A\otimes H_B\otimes H_C\to H_A\otimes H_C\otimes H_B$ be the wire permutation taking factor order $A,B,C$ to $A,C,B$ ([[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]], [[thm-qc-wire-permutation-is-unitary]]) whose unique adjoint $P^*$ exists by [[thm-adjoint-exists-and-is-unique-in-finite-dimension]], and set $\rho_{AC}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_B}(P\rho_{ABC}P^*)$, tracing out the last factor. Because $P$ is unitary, $P\rho_{ABC}P^*$ is a state: unitary conjugation preserves non-negativity by the adjoint identity ([[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]], [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]) and preserves trace by cyclicity ([[thm-trace-of-ab-equals-trace-of-ba]]). Finally set $\rho_C:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_B}\rho_{BC}$. All these marginals are density operators by applying [[lem-it-partial-traces-of-a-state-are-states]] after grouping factors. Define

$$I(A:B\mid C)_\rho:=S(\rho_{AC})+S(\rho_{BC})-S(\rho_C)-S(\rho_{ABC}).$$

These are finite-dimensional definitions only; no non-negativity of conditional entropy or conditional mutual information is part of the notation.

Let $H,K$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces, let $T:K\to K$ be positive definite, and let $V:H\to K$ satisfy $V^*V=I_H$. Then, in the non-negative operator order,

$$-\ln(V^*TV)\preceq V^*(-\ln T)V,$$

where $R\preceq S$ means $S-R$ is non-negative and logarithms of positive-definite operators are defined by finite spectral calculus.

Apply [F2] to $U,T$ and evaluate the order inequality on $A^{1/2}$ in the Hilbert-Schmidt inner product. Using [F3] on both sides yields $D(A\|B)\le\sum_i\lambda_iD(A_i\|B_i)$. exact_supplier_export.text: Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let $(E_y)_{y\in\Omega}$ be a finite POVM on $H$, where $\Omega=\{y_0,\ldots,y_{m-1}\}$ is a fixed enumeration of its nonempty outcome set. Let $K=\mathbb C^m$ with standard orthonormal basis $(f_0,\ldots,f_{m-1})$, and set $\Pi_jz:=\langle z,f_j\rangle f_j$, the rank-one projection onto $f_j$ under the root linear-first convention. The map $\mathcal M_E(X):=\sum_{j<m}\operatorname{tr}(XE_{y_j})\Pi_j$ is a quantum channel from $H$ to $K$. For the indexed register $\mathbb C^\Omega$ with orthonormal basis $|y\rangle$, the unitary identification $Jf_j=|y_j\rangle$ gives the equivalent channel $X\mapsto\sum_{y\in\Omega}\operatorname{tr}(E_yX)|y\rangle\langle y|=J\mathcal M_E(X)J^*$. Thus either finite outcome-register convention is covered.

Let $H,K$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces, let $\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ be a quantum channel ([[def-qc-quantum-channel]]), and let $A,B$ be non-negative operators on $H$. Then

$$D(\Phi(A)\|\Phi(B))\le D(A\|B).$$

$$D\!\left(\sum_i\lambda_iA_i\,\middle\|\,\sum_i\lambda_iB_i\right)\le\sum_i\lambda_iD(A_i\|B_i),$$

where zero-weight terms are omitted from the right side, and the order is that on the extended real line.

exact_supplier_export.text:
Let $\mathcal N:A\to B$ be a finite-dimensional quantum channel and use its memoryless extension $\mathcal N^{\otimes n}:A^{\otimes n}\to B^{\otimes n}$. Rates use natural logarithms, so they are in nats per channel use. For code sizes $K_n\ge1$, a rate $R\ge0$ is achievable when $\liminf_{n\to\infty}n^{-1}\ln K_n\ge R$ and the relevant error terms below tend to zero; each capacity is the supremum of its achievable rates.

For **quantum transmission**, a block code consists of an isometric encoder $W_n:M_n\to A^{\otimes n}$ and a quantum-channel decoder $\mathcal D_n:B^{\otimes n}\to M_n$, where $\dim M_n=K_n$. Let $R_n\cong M_n$ and let $|\Phi_{K_n}\rangle\in R_n\otimes M_n$ be a normalized maximally entangled vector. Its entanglement fidelity is

$$F_n:=\langle\Phi_{K_n}|(\operatorname{id}_{R_n}\otimes\mathcal D_n\mathcal N^{\otimes n}\mathcal W_n)(|\Phi_{K_n}\rangle\langle\Phi_{K_n}|)|\Phi_{K_n}\rangle,$$

where $\mathcal W_n(X)=W_nXW_n^*$. A rate is quantum-achievable if $F_n\to1$; the resulting capacity is $Q(\mathcal N)$. This is the subspace entanglement-transmission convention.

For **private classical transmission**, a block code uses equiprobable messages $m\in[K_n]$, input states $\rho_{m,n}$ on $A^{\otimes n}$, and a decoding POVM $\{\Lambda_{m,n}\}_{m=1}^{K_n}$ on $B^{\otimes n}$. Its average error is

$$e_n:=1-\frac1{K_n}\sum_{m=1}^{K_n}\operatorname{tr}(\Lambda_{m,n}\mathcal N^{\otimes n}(\rho_{m,n})).$$

Fix a complementary channel $\mathcal N^c$ as in [[def-it-quantum-channel-complement-and-coherent-information]]. Eve's average state is $\bar\tau_n=K_n^{-1}\sum_m(\mathcal N^c)^{\otimes n}(\rho_{m,n})$. Define leakage by its Holevo information

$$\ell_n:=S(\bar\tau_n)-\frac1{K_n}\sum_{m=1}^{K_n}S((\mathcal N^c)^{\otimes n}(\rho_{m,n})).$$

A rate is privately achievable when $e_n\to0$ and $\ell_n\to0$; this is strong secrecy in mutual-information form. The corresponding capacity is $P(\mathcal N)$. The value is independent of the chosen complementary dilation, as follows from [[lem-it-private-information-is-coherent-information-difference]].

For **classical transmission with prior shared entanglement**, for each block length $n$ the sender and receiver begin with a finite-dimensional shared state $\sigma_{S_AS_B}$ independent of the equiprobable message. For each $m\in[K_n]$, the sender applies a quantum channel $\mathcal E_{m,n}:\mathcal L(S_A)\to\mathcal L(A^{\otimes n})$. The receiver measures $B^{\otimes n}\otimes S_B$ with a POVM $\{\Gamma_{m,n}\}_{m=1}^{K_n}$. Its average error is

$$e_n^{EA}:=1-\frac1{K_n}\sum_{m=1}^{K_n}\operatorname{tr}\!\left[\Gamma_{m,n}\bigl((\mathcal N^{\otimes n}\circ\mathcal E_{m,n})\otimes\operatorname{id}_{S_B}\bigr)(\sigma_{S_AS_B})\right].$$ A rate is achievable when this error tends to zero; there is no constraint on the dimension or consumption of the shared entanglement. The resulting capacity is $C_E(\mathcal N)$.

The input, output, and reference registers are finite-dimensional in each block. No single-letter formula is included in these operational definitions.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space of dimension $d$, and let $\rho$ be a density operator on $H$. Then

$$S(\rho)\le\ln d,$$

with equality if and only if $\rho=I_H/d$.

$$Q(\mathcal N)=P(\mathcal N)=\max_{\rho\in\mathcal D(A)}I_c(\rho,\mathcal N),$$

and both regularizations in the quantum and private capacity formulas collapse to this one-use maximum.

Let $\mathcal N:A\to B$ be a finite-dimensional quantum channel. Under the shared-entanglement coding convention in [[def-it-quantum-channel-operational-capacities]],

$$C_E(\mathcal N)=\max_{\rho\in\mathcal D(A)}\bigl(S(\rho)+I_c(\rho,\mathcal N)\bigr)=\max_{\rho\in\mathcal D(A)}I(R;B)_{(\operatorname{id}_R\otimes\mathcal N)(\psi_\rho)},$$

where $\psi_\rho$ is any finite purification of $\rho$ on $R\otimes A$. The value is additive: $C_E(\mathcal N_1\otimes\mathcal N_2)=C_E(\mathcal N_1)+C_E(\mathcal N_2)$ for finite-dimensional channels.

$$q_n(\mathcal N):=\sup_{\rho\in\mathcal D(A^{\otimes n})}I_c(\rho,\mathcal N^{\otimes n}).$$

$$Q(\mathcal N)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{q_n(\mathcal N)}n=\sup_{n\ge1}\frac{q_n(\mathcal N)}n.$$

No general single-letter or additivity assertion is made.

$$P(\mathcal N)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{p_n(\mathcal N)}n=\sup_{n\ge1}\frac{p_n(\mathcal N)}n.$$

exact_supplier_export.text:
All logarithms are natural. First, for every density operator $\rho$ on a nonzero finite-dimensional space and every $\delta>0$, there are spectral projectors $\Pi_n$ for $\rho^{\otimes n}$ such that, as $n\to\infty$,
$$\operatorname{tr}(\Pi_n\rho^{\otimes n})\to1,\qquad \operatorname{rank}\Pi_n\le e^{n(S(\rho)+\delta)},\qquad \Pi_n\rho^{\otimes n}\Pi_n\preceq e^{-n(S(\rho)-\delta)}\Pi_n.$$

Second, let $\mathcal X$ be a finite nonempty set, let $(p_x)_{x\in\mathcal X}$ be a probability vector, and let $\sigma_x$ be density operators on a nonzero finite-dimensional output space. Put $\bar\sigma=\sum_xp_x\sigma_x$ and $H(B|X)=\sum_{x:p_x>0}p_xS(\sigma_x)$. For every $\delta>0$, there are sets $T_n\subseteq\mathcal X^n$ with $p^{\otimes n}(T_n)\to1$, global spectral projectors $\Pi_n$ for $\bar\sigma^{\otimes n}$, and conditional spectral projectors $\Pi_{x^n}$ for $\bigotimes_i\sigma_{x_i}$, such that one sequence $u_n\to0$ satisfies, for every sufficiently large $n$ and every $x^n\in T_n$,
$$\operatorname{tr}(\Pi_n\bar\sigma^{\otimes n})\to1,\quad \operatorname{tr}(\Pi_n\bigotimes_i\sigma_{x_i})\ge1-u_n,\quad \operatorname{tr}(\Pi_{x^n}\bigotimes_i\sigma_{x_i})\ge1-u_n,$$
$$\operatorname{rank}\Pi_n\le e^{n(S(\bar\sigma)+\delta)},\quad \Pi_n\bar\sigma^{\otimes n}\Pi_n\preceq e^{-n(S(\bar\sigma)-\delta)}\Pi_n,$$
$$\operatorname{rank}\Pi_{x^n}\le e^{n(H(B|X)+\delta)},\quad \Pi_{x^n}\left(\bigotimes_i\sigma_{x_i}\right)\Pi_{x^n}\preceq e^{-n(H(B|X)-\delta)}\Pi_{x^n}.$$
Zero eigenvalues are omitted from surprisal sums. No identical-distribution assumption is made for the conditional eigenbasis measurements.

exact_consumer_facts: [F2] [[lem-it-cq-typical-projector-dimension]]: the spectral typical projector for $\rho^{\otimes n}$ has mass tending to one, rank at most $e^{n(S(\rho)+\delta)}$, and every included eigenvalue is at most $e^{-n(S(\rho)-\delta)}$.
actual_proof_uses: 1.2 Suppose $\limsup_n n^{-1}\ln M_n<S(\rho)$. Choose $\delta>0$ and $N$ so that $M_n\le e^{n(S(\rho)-2\delta)}$ for $n\ge N$. Let $\Pi_n$ be the typical projector from [F2], and let $\epsilon_n=1-\operatorname{tr}(\rho^{\otimes n}\Pi_n)\to0$. Each eigenvalue in its range is at most $e^{-n(S(\rho)-\delta)}$. Therefore the sum of any $M_n$ eigenvalues of $\rho^{\otimes n}$ is at most $\epsilon_n+M_ne^{-n(S(\rho)-\delta)}\le\epsilon_n+e^{-n\delta}\to0$: the part outside the typical range contributes at most its total mass, and each selected eigenvalue inside contributes at most the displayed maximum. [F2, given, algebra, choose]

2.1 Since $r_n\le e^{n(S(\rho)+\delta)}$ and $e^{n(S+\delta)}\ge1$, $M_n=r_n+1\le2e^{n(S(\rho)+\delta)}$. Hence $\limsup_n n^{-1}\ln M_n\le S(\rho)+\delta$. Given $R>S(\rho)$, choose $\delta<R-S(\rho)$ to obtain the direct assertion. [F2, step 1.1, algebra, choose]
